column6: The capital of the Hittite empire, whose archives hold the cult inventories and ritual texts.
A cult centre north of Hattusa, sacred to a local storm god and supplied from Hattusa with offerings.
The Hittite sites were burned at the end of the empire.

column3: The Hittites create an empire centred in Anatolia; the king is also priest, and the gods are many.
Local cults keep their own storm-gods, and the queen and priestess Puduhepa works to organise and rationalise the religion.
The Hittite empire ends and its sites are burned; little of its myth survives.
